extracted.intended_audience: artists/illustrators, authors, publishers, and submitters of children's picture books; ALSC award committee members and librarians involved in submissions
extracted.subtask_description: Official terms, definitions, eligibility rules, evaluation criteria, and submission procedures for the Randolph Caldecott Medal (annual award for the most distinguished American picture book for children). Intended to guide submitters and committee members in determining eligibility and distinguishing qualities of award-worthy picture books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award recipient and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Medal shall be awarded annually to the artist of the most distinguished American picture book for children published by an American publisher in the United States in English during the preceding year. The award shall go to the artist, who must be a citizen or resident of the United States, whether or not he be the author of the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The artist may be the illustrator or co-illustrators; the artist may be awarded the medal posthumously. If a title is nominated for both Newbery and Caldecott, the committees decide under which award it will be considered. The award recognizes the artist (illustration), not didactic intent or popularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: 'American picture book in the United States' (publication origin)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'American picture book in the United States' means that books first published in previous years in other countries are not eligible. Books published simultaneously in the U.S. and another country may be eligible. Books published in a U.S. territory or U.S. commonwealth are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A book first published elsewhere in an earlier year is ineligible; simultaneous U.S./other-country publication can qualify. U.S. territories and commonwealths are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: 'In English' requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: 'In English' means that the committee considers only books written and published in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement DOES NOT limit the use of words or phrases in another language where appropriate in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: 'Published…in the preceding year' (publication date rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Published…in the preceding year' means that the book has a publication date in that year, was available for purchase in that year, and has a copyright date no later than that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A book might have a copyright date prior to the year under consideration but, for various reasons, was not published until the year under consideration. If a book is published prior to its year of copyright as stated in the book, it shall be considered in its year of copyright as stated in the book. The intent is that every book be eligible for consideration but no book be considered in more than one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: artist citizenship/residency
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is restricted to artists who are citizens or residents of the United States. 'Resident' specifies that the author has established and maintains a residence in the United States, U.S. territory, or U.S. commonwealth as distinct from being a casual or occasional visitor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residency must be an established and maintained residence, not casual visits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: 'original work' of illustration
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'original work' means that the illustrations were created by this artist and no one else. Further, 'original work' means that the illustrations are presented here for the first time and have not been previously published elsewhere in this or any other form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations reprinted or compiled from other sources are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'picture book for children'
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'picture book for children' is one that essentially provides the child with a visual experience. A picture book has a collective unity of story-line, theme, or concept, developed through the series of pictures of which the book is comprised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A picture book is for which children are an intended potential audience; it displays respect for children's understandings, abilities, and appreciations. Children are defined as persons of ages up to and including fourteen and picture books for this entire age range are to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'distinguished'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Distinguished' is defined as: Marked by eminence and distinction; noted for significant achievement. Marked by excellence in quality. Marked by conspicuous excellence or eminence. Individually distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition frames the quality threshold for medalist and honor selections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: Excellence of execution in artistic technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members need to consider excellence of execution in the artistic technique employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the technical skill and workmanship evident in the illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: Excellence of pictorial interpretation of story, theme, or concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members need to consider excellence of pictorial interpretation of story, theme, or concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how effectively the images interpret, illuminate, or enhance the underlying story, theme, or concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: Appropriateness of style of illustration to story/theme/concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members need to consider appropriateness of style of illustration to the story, theme or concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the chosen stylistic approach suits the material, audience, and intent of the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: Delineation through pictures
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members need to consider delineation of plot, theme, characters, setting, mood or information through the pictures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how clearly and effectively the illustrations convey narrative elements, character, setting, mood, or informational content without relying solely on text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: Excellence of presentation for a child audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members need to consider excellence of presentation in recognition of a child audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider readability, engagement, visual clarity, and appropriateness for children's perspectives and comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation: Acceptable graphic forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The only limitation to graphic form is that the form must be one which may be used in a picture book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphic techniques are acceptable so long as they are compatible with the picture-book format and support the child's visual experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation: Self-contained entity (no dependence on other media)
rubrics_metrics.description: The book must be a self-contained entity, not dependent on other media (i.e., sound, film or computer program) for its enjoyment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books that require external media to convey their story/presentation are ineligible; the award is for pictorial presentation within the book format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of other book components
rubrics_metrics.description: Each book is to be considered as a picture book. The committee is to make its decision primarily on the illustration, but other components of a book are to be considered especially when they make a book less effective as a children's picture book. Such other components might include the written text, the overall design of the book, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustration is primary, but poor text or design that undermines pictorial effectiveness can count against a book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award intent: not for didactic intent or popularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: The committee should keep in mind that the award is for distinguished illustrations in a picture book and for excellence of pictorial presentation for children. The award is not for didactic intent or for popularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not evaluate books on educational/didactic aims or sales/popularity when selecting medalists/honors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of committee deliberation: only eligible books and specified year
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee in its deliberations is to consider only books eligible for the award, as specified in the terms. The term 'only the books eligible for the award' specifies that the committee is not to consider the entire body of the work by an artist or whether the artist has previously won the award. The committee’s decision is to be made following deliberation about books of the specified calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should be confined to eligible titles from the relevant publication year; prior career achievements or past awards should not influence selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor books (runners-up)
rubrics_metrics.description: Honor books may be named. These shall be books that are also truly distinguished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'runners-up' changed to 'honor books' in 1971; honors are retrospective to earlier runners-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission procedure: required actions and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: How to submit books for consideration: Complete the award submission form. Mail one copy of the book to the award committee chair. The deadline for submitting works is December 31 of the publication year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address information is available upon completion of the submission form. You may attach a cover letter with contact information. There is no entry fee. ALSC membership is not required to submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission logistics and office policies
rubrics_metrics.description: The ALSC office requests that one copy of your submission be sent to the committee chair. Neither the ALSC office nor the committee chair can confirm receipt of submissions. Submissions that are dropped off in-person to the ALSC office will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you wish to confirm delivery, use a tracking number. The ALSC office cannot answer eligibility questions or advise on award eligibility—eligibility is determined by the committee and is confidential.
